newsitem.title: CHILE: CTC says costs rising faster than revenues.
newsitem.headline: CTC says costs rising faster than revenues.

text.p: Costs at Compania de Telecomunicaciones de Chile are growing faster than revenues and, barring tighter controls, "will affect all of us working at CTC," General Manager Jacinto Diaz said in a letter to employees.
A cost control campaign in the 1996 first half failed to bring the desired results, especially in the area of payments for goods and services, he said.
"In effect, figures for that period (first half 1996) show real revenue at CTC growing at a rate slower than those of operating costs," he said.
"This situation is not a passing or circumstantial component, but rather shows a trend that will not be reversed by itself."
A copy of the letter was obtained by Reuters.
CTC had no official comment on the letter, which was sent to employees on August 27.
An article in the Santiago newspaper El Mercurio quoted CTC director Fernan Ibanez as saying the letter merely showed the depth of Diaz's concern about costs.
"We all need to get better, and any manager who isn't concerned about costs is useless," Ibanez was quoted as saying. "I back the letter because it aims to improve."
In the letter, Diaz expressed concern about CTC's future if it fails to control costs better.
"We're in a position to change this projection which, if it continues and barring a sustained and systematic effort, in the long term will affect all of us working at CTC," he said.
"From my point of view, this situation has vital importance for CTC and its workers, and that's why I wanted to comment on it directly with each one of you," said the letter.
"The company's competitors are unleashing aggressive and permanent strategies to gain positions in various markets, making the most of our weaknesses," he said.

"The loss of productivity at the company, as we have said on many opportunities, not only means a step back in the face of the competition but hinders efforts at medium-term stability in the whole firm."
Daz said he wanted to make employees aware of the situation so they would appreciate the need to control costs.
"We need every worker, in whatever place, to take care of CTC's business, promote the company's services, to save, to avoid excess costs, etc.," he said in the letter.

Telefnica de Espaa owns 43 percent of CTC, which reported operating income of 54.1 billion pesos for the 1996 first half on revenues of 180.8 billion pesos, versus operating income of 46.3 billion pesos on revenues of 158 billion pesos in the first half of 1995.
